data: Work-in-progress reconstruction of the final visible state in the supplied doghole_clamp2 SolidCraft design. The active baseline keeps the low T-slide with fixed centre hinge eye, mirrored side arms, Ø3 hinge pin, 40 mm dummy rail-profile fit context and a straight Ø20 bench-dog reference. Earlier expansion-dog and compact-fork concepts remain in the retained source but are deliberately not part of this active Forge baseline.
A compact primitive model: Ø100 × 10 flange, Ø44 × 16 hub, Ø24 bore and six Ø9 bolt holes on a 70 mm PCD.
An XZ polygon extruded along Y with an edge fillet and two native SolidCraft Hole features.

One shared CornerBracket is reused by the standalone model and wooden HUB75 assemblies. Its native outline includes the 0.6 mm arm-tip relief, with inner R4 fillet, broad-face chamfers and four local triangular arm-tip wedge cuts kept editable. Four fixing seats use separate flat head recess, 90° transition, through-bore and 0.2 mm edge-relief features instead of one oversized countersink.
A constructive solid geometry demonstration: intersect a cube with a sphere, then subtract cylinders along three axes.

A printable bench dog inferred from the Mini-MFT reference image: 20 mm above and 20 mm below the worktop, with one full-length tapered insert from Ø20.0 at the worktop to Ø20.2 at the free end. A compact Ø22 stop collar seats on the 45° chamfer of a nominal Ø20 MFT hole. Two perpendicular slots create four flexible legs, with R0.5 mm relief around the central cross. The top face carries a recessed BrainBox cube/box wireframe.

A second fixed cross-section of the generic GuideRail component. The aluminium shape comes from the Makita 199141-8 STEP reference and is calibrated to the TSO measured 182.50 × 10.28 mm envelope. The standalone CAD example uses 600 mm for compact visual inspection.

The generic GuideRail component with its default Festool profile. The aluminium cross-section comes from the FS 1400/2 STEP reference and is calibrated to the TSO measured 184.20 × 10.50 mm envelope. Only rail length is a native CAD parameter.

Basic hinge reconstructed from the supplied native SolidCraft Hinge Assembly. Two identical 40 × 30 × 3 mm leaves each carry a Ø8 × 40 mm knuckle along X. Leaf A remains grounded while Leaf B is connected by a native revolute joint named Hinge, starting at 60° with 0–180° limits.

Tube-supported derivative of the accepted two-panel Display Frame. It retains the same panel grid and Middle coupler, uses the tube-ready Edge and Corner variants, and adds two 360 mm Ø10 × 1 mm aluminum tubes plus eight separate reusable tube-clamp occurrences at the source-derived datums. One shared clamp-bore dependency is controlled by an independent Installed Configuration Rule, enabled by default for the assembly.

Framed version of the existing two-panel HUB75 screen. It keeps the same 320 × 320 mm nominal two-panel grid and alternating right-panel orientation, then adds the shared Medium coupler family around the panel seam and outer frame: one middle coupler, two edge couplers and four corner couplers.

Second-generation wooden HUB75 enclosure. It keeps the 844 × 362 mm display opening and five-panel layout while adding a 70 mm clear lower compartment, a 12 mm intermediate shelf, two 12 mm dividers, full-depth side walls with hand slots, and an inset display-only rear board.
Tube-ready derivative of the accepted Medium left Corner coupler. It adds the source insertion recess, Ø10.5 tube clearance, one slide rail and its asymmetric entry chamfer.

data: Fixed Medium left corner coupler, sharing all source dimensions and helper operations with the edge/right-corner members.
Tube-ready derivative of the accepted Medium right Corner coupler. It adds the mirrored source insertion recess, Ø10.5 tube clearance, one slide rail and its asymmetric entry chamfer.

data: Fixed Medium right corner coupler. The native Medium configuration keeps its panel-pin pass-through suppressed.

Tube-ready derivative of the accepted Medium Edge coupler. It retains the base coupler geometry and adds only the final active inward clamp clearance, two rails at 40 mm center spacing, clamp-bow clearance and asymmetric rail-entry chamfers from the retained SolidCraft source.
Fixed Medium straight edge member from the shared HUB75 frame-coupler family. The native Medium panel-pin pass-through stays suppressed.

Fixed Medium port of the native middle HUB75 frame coupler. The owner shares its source data, dimensions and helpers with the edge and corner variants so the future native configuration table can be added without moving or renaming the physical CAD family.

One reusable purchased aluminum tube component shared by the top and bottom positions of the HUB75 tube-supported frame. The retained native source uses identical Ø10 mm outside / Ø8 mm inside geometry for both occurrences, so placement belongs to the assembly rather than to separate physical owners.

Shared 159.70 × 319.71 × 14.50 mm P5 HUB75 panel from the supplied hub75_improved_v2 native source. The reusable housing keeps its established local XY/Z contract for screen assemblies, while the standalone detailed model adds the refined rounded/stepped rear bays, side-wall trimming, two HUB75 data connector envelopes, the approximate power connector and four white orientation markings as separate source-derived occurrences.

Two detailed HUB75 panels placed side by side on the same 160 mm nominal pitch used by the five-panel screen. The panel centres are X=-80 and X=+80 mm at Z=160 mm. The left panel uses the normal upright placement and the right panel uses the existing alternating reversed orientation for the rear data chain. The original five-panel BasicHub75Screen remains a separate model.

Five panels on the source project’s 800 × 320 mm nominal grid. One reusable detailed panel component is reused at X=-320, -160, 0, 160 and 320 mm. Columns 2 and 4 reverse direction for the rear data chain, and all occurrences stand upright in XZ.

Source-faithful reusable tube clamp with native Free/Installed fit state. Tube diameter, clamp interference and clamp bore remain editable dependencies; Ø10 with 0.4 mm interference gives a 9.6 mm Free bore, while the independent Installed rule drives the bore to the tube diameter.

One clearly parametrized assembly: five lightweight HUB75 modules, 12 mm sidewalls/bottom/roof, 9 mm attached rear, 4 mm glass and four straight-mitred wooden retainers from one GlassStrip class. The roof extends 10 mm in front and 1 mm beyond the attached rear sheet. Eight printed corner brackets share the CornerBracket definition.

Generic matching hook/keeper for the latch. The SCPF model mirrors the supplied native SolidCraft blank and fold history directly: one fixed 2 mm sheet blank with two Ø4.3 mounting holes followed by one R2.1 fold. The native hook source is preserved beside the reconstruction.

Generic latch component reconstructed from the original native SolidCraft design. The authoritative source is preserved at reference/latch.sc. The mechanism combines a 2 mm mounting foot, 1.6 mm operating handle, 2 mm pull bail, 0.7 mm locking spring/lip, hinge pins and revolved rivets. The released Forge sheet-metal and revolve primitives reproduce the native feature history without fused-solid approximations.

Native-source MFT rail corner subassembly. Two 150 mm MountingRailM8 pieces meet at 90 degrees with their C-openings facing outward. The structural PETG bracket fixes and supports both rail ends. A separate replaceable PETG corner insert fills the exposed outside corner and clips into place with two integral retaining lips. The bracket rail holes align with the first and second round perforations, while the top gusset exposes the MFT underside screw seat.

Prototype monolithic corner bracket for the Simple MFT support frame. Two perpendicular 75 mm arms bolt through the existing round rail perforations at 12.5 mm and 62.5 mm from each rail end. Two 6 mm-thick plastic shoes continue underneath the rail profiles so the rails actually rest on the bracket. The two shoes meet through the exact R18 lower outside-corner sector from the native source. Exposed corner filling/protection is now owned by the separate MFT Rail Corner Insert. Upper and lower triangular gussets stiffen the corner. The upper gusset includes one provisional countersunk fixing hole into the underside of the MFT worktop.

Separate printable insert from the native MFT corner assembly. The part fills and rounds the exposed outside corner between the two perpendicular mounting rails. Its source outline uses an exact R18 outer quarter arc, an inner rounded notch and two integral clip lips with sloped lead-ins. The insert is kept separate from the structural rail bracket so it can be printed or replaced independently.

A reusable light mounting-rail component authored in fabrication order as native sheet metal: developed flat blank, four source perforations, one repeated native feature pattern and four 90-degree folds. The supplied DRESSELHAUS/HORNBACH product establishes 1000 mm length, galvanized steel, M8 use and 1.25 mm thickness. The 27 × 18 mm section and perforation dimensions use a generic published 27/18 rail reference and are not claimed as DRESSELHAUS manufacturing dimensions.
Reconstructs the Raspberry Pi 4 video using a rounded open-top shell, mounting bosses, connector cuts, floor vents, Pi 4 lettering and PETG material.
Rebuilds the supplied enclosure with the normal SCPF Box sketch/extrusion, followed by native Shell, Lip, Snap Fit, Boss and Rest features.
A feature-based plate: box, four vertical fillets and four through holes.
Builds a centered plate with native Base, Holes and Bore sketches. One parameter-driven Ø8 hole cut is repeated by a native rectangular pattern, while a Ø24 boss is joined between the two cuts.

Native Forge reconstruction of the SolidCraft default Sheet Metal Bracket. A 120 × 60 mm flat blank uses the Steel 2mm rule, then receives two 30 mm 90° inside flanges, one 20 mm 60° inside flange and an 8 mm hem. The model intentionally preserves native sheet-metal history and rule inheritance so it also exercises Forge’s sheet-metal support and recoverable flat pattern.
Minimal model proving that one independent model root can be authored with Forge and built without repository-specific Python orchestration.

The 805 mm Simple MFT worktop is extended on the right by a plain 195 × 555 × 18 mm plank, creating a 1000 mm-wide work surface. Two long M8 mounting rails run underneath and are shifted 18 mm right to meet a third 519 mm cross rail on the left short side without blocking the channel ends. All C-openings face outward. The 800 mm Festool-profile GuideRail is shifted 414 mm toward +X. A reusable FlexBenchDog is inserted in the bottom hole of the rightmost MFT column at X=+304 mm, Y=-228 mm. MDF, galvanized-steel and aluminium materials distinguish the assembly visually.

A reusable CRAFTMAKER-inspired worktop component: one 18 mm native Box, four straight 20 mm corner chamfers, 59 Ø20 dog holes on the nominal 9 × 7 / 76 mm grid with the four diagonal ring-2 positions omitted, and eight photo-measured native diagonal Slots.
Recreates the SolidCraft Vent Plate example with a rounded 120 × 80 × 4 mm plate, one rectangular source cut and one native two-direction rectangular pattern.

Parametric reconstruction of the supplied tutorial wall hook with a native A4 landscape technical drawing. The confirmed source dimensions define the 57 mm high XZ hook profile, 15 mm symmetric Y extrusion, 6 mm walls, 20 mm hook opening, triangular gusset window and two Ø4.2 mm mounting holes through the rear 6 mm mounting wall. A separate Ø8 mm coaxial tool-access bore clears only the diagonal reinforcement in front of the lower screw so the mounting wall remains intact. Forge v0.19 applies the native 1.5 mm FRONT/BACK boundary chamfer while each screw hole keeps a 1.0 mm tool-side entry chamfer and only a 0.3 mm wall-side elephant-foot relief. The finished body receives a display-only #FFD21A yellow appearance matching the tutorial result; physical material/BOM semantics remain unchanged. The outer silhouette and triangular relief are authored as sharp polygons first, then rounded with native R2 fillet operations. Only those visible fillet radii remain explicitly inferred from the rendered reference.
